question.problem: Find the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation ${27}^{x+2}={3}^{4x}.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base.

To do this, we write $27$ as ${3}^{3},$ and then rewrite the left-hand side using the power rule of exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{27}^{x+2} & ={3}^{4x} \\ {({3}^{3})}^{x+2} & ={3}^{4x} \\ {3}^{3(x+2)} & ={3}^{4x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(3)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+2) & =4x \\ 3x+6 & =4x \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$
